root_cause_identified.expected_solution: The busy loop does not originate in ureq. ureq's src/rtls.rs wraps the socket as rustls::StreamOwned and delegates read to it; rustls's blocking Stream adapter (rustls/src/stream.rs, Stream::read) calls self.conn.complete_io(self.sock) in a loop. The defect is in rustls's complete_io in rustls/src/conn.rs (repo rustls, tag v/0.21.10). Its loop keeps iterating until it is sure the exchange is finished, but there is a state where the connection wants neither to write pending TLS data nor to read more, and is not cleanly closed: the loop then does no IO and falls through its terminal match without returning, so it spins at 100% CPU forever. A peer that stalls mid-exchange without closing triggers exactly this. The agent must name rustls's complete_io as the spinning site and explain that ureq merely delegates through the boxed read-write object into rustls's blocking stream and completion loop, and that the client's read timeout never fires because the thread never returns to client code.
evaluation_criteria: Attributes the spin to rustls (the transitive/upstream repo), NOT ureq
Names rustls's blocking IO-completion routine (complete_io) as the loop that fails to terminate
Explains the no-progress state: the connection wants neither write nor read and is not cleanly closed, so the loop does no IO yet iterates again
Explains the traversal: ureq TLS stream wrapper -> rustls StreamOwned/Stream::read -> complete_io loop

patch_lands_at_fix_site.expected_solution: The agent leaves an uncommitted diff in /workspace/rustls that modifies rustls/src/conn.rs at the complete_io loop, matching the upstream fix (rustls commit ebcb4782f23b on the 0.21 line). A diff that only touches ureq, or that adds a wall-clock timeout in the client, is not the correct site.
evaluation_criteria: git diff in the rustls workspace repo shows a modification to the blocking IO-completion routine (conn.rs / complete_io)
The change is in rustls, not ureq
No new files; an in-place edit of the existing completion loop

patch_bails_on_no_progress.expected_solution: The patch makes the completion loop return when neither a write nor a read is wanted, exactly as the upstream fix does with `if !self.wants_write() && !self.wants_read() { return Ok((rdlen, wrlen)); }` at the top of the loop. An equivalent no-progress guard that returns instead of looping again is acceptable. A wall-clock timeout, a sleep, or a bounded retry counter is not the correct fix.
evaluation_criteria: The diff adds a guard on wants_write and wants_read (no-progress detection) inside the completion loop
In the no-progress state the loop returns instead of iterating again
The fix is scoped to the completion loop, not a timeout bolted on elsewhere
